{{short description|Professor of Molecular Biophysics}}
{{Infobox scientist/Wikidata|fetchwikidata=ALL|suppressfields=works}}
'''Elspeth Frances Garman''' is a retired professor of [[molecular biophysics]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and a former President of the [[British Crystallographic Association]].<ref name="BCA">{{cite web |title=Archive of previous BCA Councils  |url=https://www.crystallography.org.uk/about/previous-councils/ |publisher=[[British Crystallographic Association]] |accessdate=2015-09-24}}</ref> Until 2021 she was also Senior Kurti Research Fellow at [[Brasenose College, Oxford]],<ref name="Brasenose">{{cite web |url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/alumni/recordings/2410-pc-15062021 |title=Principal's Conversations: Professor Elspeth Garman  |publisher=[[Brasenose College, Oxford]] |accessdate=2023-10-09}}</ref> where she is now an emeritus fellow.<ref>{{cite web |title=Emeritus Fellows |url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/academic-staff/emeritus-fellows |publisher=[[Brasenose College, Oxford]] |access-date=7 February 2024}}</ref> The "Garman limit", which is the [[Absorbed dose|radiation dose limit]] of a [[Cryochemistry|cryocooled]] [[protein crystal]], is [[Eponym|named after her]].

==Education and career==
Garman studied [[physics]] at [[Durham University]] and then moved to [[Linacre College, Oxford]], for a doctorate in [[nuclear physics]] supervised by [[Kenneth Allen (physicist)|Kenneth Allen]] which she completed in 1980.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Garman |first=Elspeth Frances |title=Inelastic alpha particle scattering from <sup>16</sup>O and medium mass nuclei in the incident energy range 7-18 MeV |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?vid=OXVU1&search_scope=LSCOP_OX&docId=oxfaleph012153095&fn=permalink |publisher=Thesis DPhil -- University of Oxford |date=1980}}</ref> She taught at [[Lincoln College, Oxford|Lincoln College]], [[St Hilda's College, Oxford|St Hilda's College]], [[St Anne's College, Oxford|St Anne's College]], [[Somerville College, Oxford|Somerville College]], and [[Worcester College, Oxford|Worcester College]], and switched to [[biophysics]] in 1987. Since then, she has co-authored more than 150 [[Protein Data Bank]] entries and contributed to techniques for macromolecular structure determination.<ref name="EFG2014">{{cite journal |last=Garman |first=Elspeth F. |title=Developments in x-ray crystallographic structure determination of biological macromolecules |journal=Science |volume=343 |issue=6175 |pages=1102–1108 |year=2014 |pmid=24604194 |doi=10.1126/science.1247829 |bibcode=2014Sci...343.1102G|s2cid=21067016 }}</ref> In particular, Garman has been amongst the pioneers of cryoprotection of macromolecular crystals<ref name="EFG2003">{{cite book |last1=Garman |first1=Elspeth F. |author2-link=Sylvie Doublié |last2=Doublié |first2=Sylvie |chapter=Cryocooling of Macromolecular Crystals: Optimization Methods |title=Macromolecular Crystallography, Part C |series=Methods in Enzymology |volume=368 |pages=188–216|year=2003|doi=10.1016/S0076-6879(03)68011-0|pmid=14674275|isbn=9780121822712}}<!--|accessdate=2015-11-13 --></ref> and has made major contributions to the study of the damage that X-rays induce in macromolecular crystals. In a seminal paper in 2006, Garman and collaborators established the radiation dose limit for [[Cryochemistry|cryocooled]] [[protein crystal]]s, which was named the "Garman limit" after her.<ref name="EFG2006">{{cite journal |last1=Owen |first1=Robin Leslie |last2=Rudiño-Piñera |first2=Enrique |last3=Garman |first3=Elspeth F. |title=Experimental determination of the radiation dose limit for cryocooled protein crystals |journal=PNAS USA |volume=103 |issue=13 |pages=4912–4917 |year=2006 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0600973103 |pmid=16549763 |bibcode=2006PNAS..103.4912O |pmc=1458769|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2025, Garman and Nicola Laurieri published ''Mathematics for Biosciences: From Theory to Worked Examples and Applications'', an undergraduate textbook covering mathematical methods and applications in the biosciences.<ref>{{cite book
 |last1=Garman
 |first1=Elspeth F.
 |last2=Laurieri
 |first2=Nicola
 |title=Mathematics for Biosciences: From Theory to Worked Examples and Applications
 |publisher=World Scientific
 |year=2025
 |doi=10.1142/Q0473
 |isbn=978-1-80061-603-5
}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2014, she was awarded the Rose Lecture and Medal at [[Kingston University]]<ref name="RL2014">{{cite web |title=Rose Lecture Series: How a century of X-ray crystallography has changed the world |url=https://www.kingston.ac.uk/events/item/1085/24-jun-2014-rose-lecture-series-how-a-century-of-xray-crystallography-has-changed-the-world/ |publisher=[[Kingston University]] |date=24 June 2014 |accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref> and the Humanitarian Award of the Women's International Film and Television Showcase.<ref>{{cite web |title=Student Blog: Interviewing Elspeth Garman |url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/news/1704-student-blog-interviewing-elspeth-garman |publisher=[[Brasenose College, Oxford]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> In 2015 she received the [[Mildred Dresselhaus]] Senior Award and guest professorship at the [[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging]].<ref name="MD2015">{{cite web |url=http://www.cui.uni-hamburg.de/en/2015/07/mildred-dresselhaus-awardees-2015-selected/ |title=Mildred Dresselhaus Awardees 2015 selected |publisher=[[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging]] |accessdate=2015-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117063442/http://www.cui.uni-hamburg.de/en/2015/07/mildred-dresselhaus-awardees-2015-selected/ |archive-date=2015-11-17 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016 she received the [[Isidor Fankuchen|I. Fankuchen]] Award of the [[American Crystallographic Association]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fankuchen Memorial Award |url=https://www.amercrystalassn.org/fankuchen-memorial-award |publisher=[[American Crystallographic Association]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref><ref name="OxFankuchen">{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Julian |title=2016 American Crystallographic Association Fankuchen Award for Elspeth Garman |url=http://www.bioch.ox.ac.uk/aspsite/index.asp?pageid=1300 |publisher=Department of Biochemistry, University of Oxford |date=2015-11-19 |accessdate=2015-11-20 |archive-date=2015-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121021152/http://www.bioch.ox.ac.uk/aspsite/index.asp?pageid=1300 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{citation |last=American Crystallographic Association |title=Elspeth Garman, Fankuchen Award Lecture, 2016 ACA Annual Meeting, Denver |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SqArDVbc5-I |date=2017-04-04 |accessdate=2018-01-14}}</ref> In 2008 she was awarded Major Educator by the University of Oxford. In 2014 she was awarded Most Acclaimed Lecturer Award by [[Oxford University Student Union|OUSU]] as well as an 'Individual Teaching Award' from Mathematical, Physical and Life Sciences (MPLS) Division.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Biography - Elspeth Garman |url=https://history.amercrystalassn.org/h-elspeth-garman-memoir |publisher=[[American Crystallographic Association]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Lab Talk |url=http://newsletters.medsci.ox.ac.uk/september-2014/lab-talk |work=MSD Newsletters |access-date=2018-01-14 |archive-date=2017-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826224424/http://newsletters.medsci.ox.ac.uk/september-2014/lab-talk/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Garman is the first recipient of the Sosei Heptares Prize, awarded in July 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=British Biophysical Society Biennial Meeting |url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/british-biophysical-society-biennial-meeting-olwyn-byron |date=2018-05-29 |access-date=2018-07-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2018 Sosei Heptares Prize for Biophysics to be awarded to Prof Elspeth Garman |url=https://www.bioch.ox.ac.uk/article/2018-sosei-heptares-prize-for-biophysics-awarded-to-prof-elspeth-garman |publisher=Department of Biochemistry, University of Oxford |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> She received an honorary doctorate from Durham University in July 2019.<ref name="DurhamDoc">{{cite web |url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/about-us/professional-services/ceremonies/honorary-degrees/past-honorary-degrees/#DSc |title=Honorary Degrees |work=Ceremonies |publisher=Durham University |accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref> In August 2019, the European Crystallographic Association awarded her the 11th Max Perutz Prize.<ref name="ECA Perutz Prize">{{cite web |url=https://ecanews.org/blog/eleventh-eca-max-perutz-prize-to-professor-elspeth-garman/|title=Prizes |work=Ceremonies |date=17 June 2019 |publisher=European Crystallographic Association |accessdate=2019-08-18}}</ref> She was elected Fellow of the American Crystallographic Association in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amercrystalassn.org/fellows|title=Fellows}}</ref> In 2020 she was awarded the Suffrage Science Life Sciences Award.<ref name="Suffrage Science Life Sciences Award">{{cite web |url=https://www.suffragescience.org/post/life-sciences-awardee-2020-professor-elspeth-garman|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211180320/https://www.suffragescience.org/post/life-sciences-awardee-2020-professor-elspeth-garman|url-status=usurped|archive-date=February |access-date=7 February 2024}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
Garman has been involved in over 40 TV and radio programmes.<ref name=":0" /> In December 2017, she gave a talk as part of the Illuminating Atoms exhibition&nbsp;at the [[Royal Albert Hall]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Hogenboom |first=Melissa |title=Crystal beauty: Illuminating the structure of matter |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-29952311 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |date=2014-11-10 |access-date=2018-01-14}}</ref> In 2014 she was interviewed for [[BBC Radio 4]]'s programme ''[[The Life Scientific]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elspeth Garman on crystallography, The Life Scientific |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04kbjhg |publisher=BBC Radio 4 |access-date=2018-01-14}}</ref> Garman also helped produce a video with the [[Royal Institution]] about "Understanding Crystallography".<ref>{{citation |last=The Royal Institution |title=Understanding Crystallography - Part 1: From Proteins to Crystals |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gLsC4wlrR2A |date=2014-04-02 |accessdate=2018-01-14}}</ref> In 2014 she helped to create an animated video with Oxford Sparks on crystallography.<ref>{{citation |title=Oxford Sparks: A Case of Crystal Clarity |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z7hXiKiZZPs |date=2014-03-18 |accessdate=2018-01-14}}</ref> In 2010 she gave the [[Dorothy Hodgkin]] Memorial Lecture "Crystallography One Century AD (after Dorothy)".<ref name="DH2010">{{cite web |last=Cooper |first=Richard |title=Dorothy Hodgkin Memorial Lecture 2010 |url=http://www.crystallography.org.uk/dorothy-hodgkin-memorial-lecture-2010/ |publisher=[[British Crystallographic Association]] |date=2010-05-14 |accessdate=2015-11-08 |archive-date=2015-11-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117020237/http://www.crystallography.org.uk/dorothy-hodgkin-memorial-lecture-2010/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2016 she gave the inaugural [[Rosalind Franklin]] memorial lecture as well as the inaugural [[William Lawrence Bragg|Lawrence Bragg]] memorial lecture.<ref>{{citation |last=Birkbeck, University of London |title=[Rosalind Franklin Lecture 2016] What crystallography has done for the world |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1K1pXXlumbk |date=2016-06-06 |accessdate=2018-01-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Events |url=http://www.physics.manchester.ac.uk/news-and-events/events/inaugural-external-bragg-lecture.htm |publisher=The University of Manchester {{!}} School of Physics and Astronomy |access-date=2018-01-14}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Garman married John James Barnett (1947–2010), an atmospheric physicist, in January 1979.<ref>{{cite news |title=John Barnett |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/john-barnett-h5tfgb63zkb |work=[[The Times]] |date=2010-08-20 |access-date=2018-01-14 |issn=0140-0460}}</ref> There are three daughters.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Shine |first=Keith P. |title=John J. Barnett |journal=Weather |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=27 |date=2011-01-01 |issn=1477-8696 |bibcode=2011Wthr...66...27S |doi=10.1002/wea.738 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Garman is a keen rower, and obtained a rowing half-blue in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Elspeth Garman - Brasenose College, Oxford |url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/academic-staff/437-professor-elspeth-garman |website=www.bnc.ox.ac.uk}}</ref>
